scope: Two explicitly requested examples: Harvard PowerAgent roadmap/community and University of Vermont PowerDAG. No shared content or renderer edits; no experiments rerun.

poweragent.name: PowerAgent
poweragent.identity: Harvard SEAS Power and AI Initiative's open-source community and three-layer roadmap, introduced by Qian Zhang and Le Xie in 2025; not the later PowerAgentBench-Dyn paper.

paper.title: PowerAgent: A Road Map Toward Agentic Intelligence in Power Systems: Foundation Model, Model Context Protocol, and Workflow
paper.affiliation: Harvard John A. Paulson School of Engineering and Applied Sciences
paper.full_text_access: Publisher returns an access error; TechRxiv returns403; indexed author-PDF CloudFront host no longer resolves. Only indexed portions of the author preprint were accessible. Do not claim the complete journal article was inspected.
paper.alternative_full_primary: The full19-page Le Xie ERCOT presentation (8December2025) was inspected; it cites this paper and presents the roadmap and demonstrations. Current author project/site/repositories independently support the concrete implementation examples.

poweragent.relationship_to_P01: PowerAgentBench-Dyn (arXiv2606.20401, existing P01) is a later benchmark contribution within the PowerAgent ecosystem, measuring constrained dynamic-study tasks. It is not the original PowerAgent roadmap, and its session results must retain their P01 attribution.

layers.name: PowerFM
layers.function: Domain knowledge and reasoning: retrieval, fine-tuning, domain foundation models and evaluation

layers.name: PowerMCP
layers.function: Standardized interfaces that expose power software/tools to an agent

layers.name: PowerWF
layers.function: Multi-step study orchestration and human–machine workflow design

poweragent.later_component: The current project also names PowerSkills, a library of domain instructions. Distinguish the current ecosystem from the2025 paper's three-layer roadmap.
poweragent.roadmap_locator: PA03 PDF p.11; Harvard project overview PA02
poweragent.demonstration_scope: Load-growth or large-load grid impact: examine congestion, voltage and N−1 contingencies, and draft a study report with mitigation suggestions. PA03 pp.13–14 and current PA02 demonstrations.

current_implementation.status: Author example source inspected; not executed or independently performance-tested
current_implementation.framework: Explicit LangGraph StateGraph and ToolNode imports; LangChain ChatOpenAI wrapper
current_implementation.model: Current example names gpt-4o in code; do not generalize this to every PowerAgent component or the historical article
current_implementation.simulator: PowerWorld tool groups imported by this graph; a separate pandapower module also exists, but this graph uses the PowerWorld groups
main_stage_order: add load and run modified power flow
current_implementation.state_and_routing: Four completion flags route the shared tools node back to the appropriate analysis node. Conditional edges let analysis nodes request tools before proceeding.
current_implementation.authority_caveat: Source is a demonstration workflow. Tool return interpretation/completion flags are not independent engineering acceptance, utility approval or live-control authorization.

code_and_tools.tool_examples: PowerMCP currently exposes servers including PSS/E, PowerWorld, OpenDSS, pandapower and PowerFactory. Proprietary engines still require the user's installation/license; an MCP wrapper does not grant software access.

poweragent.numerical_result_caveat: The roadmap, author presentation and inspected source example do not establish a matched success-rate or speedup trial for this workflow. Do not borrow P01 dynamic-benchmark results as original PowerAgent performance or plot an invented percentage.

powerdag.title: PowerDAG: Supervisory Agentic AI System for Automating Distribution Grid Analysis
powerdag.affiliation: Department of Electrical and Biomedical Engineering, University of Vermont, Burlington, VT, USA
powerdag.version_warning: Search results often expose v1's old Reliable title, GPT-5.2 and100% result. Do not mix these with v4's larger benchmark, newer models and98% result.
powerdag.maturity: Research prototype and controlled workflow benchmark on feeder models; not live utility-control deployment
powerdag.framework_attribution: Custom paper architecture with six evaluated configurations. LangChain ReAct and CrewAI are comparison configurations; no evidence establishes the full PowerDAG system as LangGraph.

mechanisms.name: Adaptive retrieval
steps: Rank50 archived expert query-workflow records by query-embedding cosine similarity.
Fit a two-segment score-decay elbow to select a query-specific candidate count.
Run an LLM filter once on candidate query/workflow traces; retain existing useful exemplars rather than generating a plan in this filter.
mechanisms.locator: Section IV.B; Figure3, PDF p.4; AppendixC–E,p.9

mechanisms.name: JIT supervision
steps: Obtain proposed tool name and bound arguments.
Check the rule library for required preceding Write tools.
If a required prerequisite is absent, block before execution, preserve environment state and return a corrective advisory.
If covered prerequisites pass, or a tool has no rule, allow the call.
mechanisms.locator: Section IV.C, PDF pp.4–5; Algorithm1,p.5; AppendixF,pp.9–10

powerdag.dag_semantics: DAG nodes represent individual call events, not tool types. Repeated uses of one tool are distinct nodes in an acyclic event trace. The enclosing propose/observe/supervise execution loop remains iterative; this does not mean every runtime control graph is acyclic.

verified_tool_sequence.query: Run steady-state three-phase power flow on Stowe at2025-03-21 09:00, then plot bus-voltage magnitudes
verified_tool_sequence.diagram_instruction: Depict this as the reported exemplar ordering, not a proven minimal prerequisite DAG. Group the three data loaders as a preparation block and constraints/objective as an assembly block if needed, but do not introduce unverified parallelism or additional PV/BESS scenario edges.
verified_tool_sequence.strict_gate_example: SectionIV.C p.5 explicitly gives voltage-violation checking after a power-flow solve as a prerequisite. Introduction pp.1–2 explains that skipping a prerequisite network-state update can let a solver return success on the wrong state.
verified_tool_sequence.unverified_example: No exact base-model→PV/BESS-scenario prerequisite chain is established in the v4 paper text; do not invent one.

benchmark.location: Four real-world Vermont distribution feeders represented as GridLAB-D models, with coordinates and AMI load series
benchmark.grid_bus_counts: Not disclosed in the inspected v4; do not infer topology sizes
benchmark.split: Within-family holdout; test queries differ in feeder/parameters/time/solver/limits/artifacts but share studied task families with the exemplars.

metrics.Pass_at_1: Fraction of150 held-out queries whose executed workflows cover all required expert calls, compatible arguments and valid dependency order. Additional Read calls are tolerated; extra state-changing Write calls fail except limit setters deduplicated to final values.
metrics.Precision: Fraction of queries with expert-equivalent workflow after DAG normalization; not conventional per-call precision and not the same as Pass@1.
metrics.tokens: Mean prompt+completion tokens over successful runs for TableII, shown in thousands. All-run averages reported separately are not interchangeable.

table_II.locator: TableII, PDF p.8 (TableI,p.6 only defines configuration components)

selected_same_model_ablation.count_status: Counts reconstructed from reported percentages and explicitly stated n=150; percentages are author-reported. No new experiment or repeated-trial interval.
selected_same_model_ablation.caption: GPT-5.5 workflow success on the same150 held-out queries: retrieval and prerequisite checks are complementary in this benchmark. One run per query/configuration; published v4 TableII.
selected_same_model_ablation.extra_metric_caution: Full GPT-5.5 PowerDAG has98.00% Pass@1 but47.33% expert-equivalent Precision; do not describe98% as exact tool-trace replication.
selected_same_model_ablation.token_caveat: These are rounded TableII means over successful runs only, not dollars or all-attempt total cost.

supervisor_coverage.limitation: Uncovered tools are allowed, and required-tool membership does not certify all possible parameter/freshness/physics constraints. The encoded rule set is not exhaustive.

implementation.agent_status: Paper-linked repository; current content could not be fetched in this review
implementation.benchmark_status: Author README, task structure, tool manifest and evaluator interface verified; not executed
implementation.public_reproducibility: Feeder network data, GIS data and network-tool implementations are proprietary and omitted. Only BESS/basicPV/GFI (3of10 families) are fully runnable from the public install. All ground-truth workflow JSON remains available.
implementation.old_repository_warning: The v1-linked PowerDAG/PowerDAG repository README uses a generic PowerAgent package name. Do not confuse that package with Harvard's separate Power-Agent organization, or assume it reproduces v4.

limitations: One run per model/configuration/query; no run-to-run uncertainty estimate.
Held-out queries share the ten task families and four feeder models; this does not establish unseen-family or arbitrary-utility generalization.
Pass@1 is expert-workflow conformance, not an independent field-safety probability or end-to-end operator productivity measure.
No public reconstruction of all9,000 runs is possible without proprietary network software/data.
Do not generalize correct prerequisite checks to complete physical validation or authorization.
Baseline framework results concern the paper's configured tasks and implementation; they do not rank every possible LangChain or CrewAI application.

proposed_slides.title: PowerDAG learns a workflow from expert examples
points: Adaptive retrieval selects expert query/tool traces; a one-time filter checks procedural relevance.
The model still proposes calls, while an external supervisor checks prerequisites.
proposed_slides.visual: Query → exemplar selection → agent → gate → environment; observations and advisories return to agent

proposed_slides.title: A voltage plot depends on a solved, updated model
points: The published Stowe exemplar loads inputs, builds and solves a model, updates voltages, then plots.
Call events form a DAG; repeating a tool creates a new event rather than a cyclic prerequisite.

proposed_slides.title: A supervisor blocks missing prerequisites before execution
points: A missing prerequisite yields an advisory and leaves the environment unchanged.
Rules cover94of108 tools; unlisted tools are not automatically blocked.
